title: Gears, motor and first power
target: Compare a gear-based prediction with a supervised first powered test.
criteria: Check gear mesh and secure connections before power.
Calculate ideal wheel speed from measured or supplied rpm.
Document first-test evidence and one revision.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Before first power, gears bind during a slow hand check with power disconnected. Which action is appropriate?
options: Power the motor harder until teeth bend.
Record successful operation without testing.
Correct the mesh and clearance before a supervised powered test.
Put a finger between powered gears.
cpa.guide: A binding drivetrain should be corrected before power is applied.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A wire can touch an exposed rotating gear. Which first-test preparation addresses the risk?
options: Secure and insulate the wiring away from the gear’s full motion.
Remove the switch so testing is faster.
Rest the wire on the teeth.
Hold the wire by hand during the powered run.
cpa.guide: Secure routing prevents entanglement and electrical faults without hands near motion.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 16-tooth motor gear turns at 480 rpm and drives a 48-tooth axle gear. What is axle rate?
options: 30 rpm
480 rpm
160 rpm
cpa.guide: 480 × 16/48 = 160 rpm; the larger driven gear turns more slowly.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: The wheel rate is 150 rpm and circumference is 0.28 m. What is ideal no-slip speed?
options: 42 m/s
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: On a first supervised run, the motor turns but the driven gear does not. Which record and next step best use that evidence?
options: Reach into the gears while powered.
Assume the battery is empty despite motor rotation.
Record the observation, disconnect power, and inspect gear engagement.
Record “perfect run” and continue racing.
cpa.guide: The observation points to transmission/engagement; inspect safely before concluding a cause.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: Which first-test note separates observation from explanation?
options: “Axle spun at 200 rpm,” when it was not timed.
“Motor rotates; axle is still. Possible loose coupling; inspect after disconnecting power.”
“The car is bad.”
“Teacher approved,” before a checkpoint.
cpa.guide: The first statement records visible evidence and labels the proposed cause as tentative.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
